Every stored or transmitted IV must carry the clock tag; any comparison, ratio, or term-structure calculation between two IVs with different clock tags must raise, not coerce.

Compute T from a per-symbol expiry instant read from configuration, defaulting to 16:00:00 America/New_York, not 16:15. Clamp T to zero at or past that instant. Assert T > 0 before any log or division; if T <= 0 return terminal-payoff values (delta = +/-1 or 0 by intrinsic, gamma = vega = theta = 0) tagged 'expired', and never feed them to a solver.

Solve for total variance w = sigma*sqrt(T), never for sigma directly. Use the derivative dPrice/dw = S*exp(-q*T)*phi(d1) (which stays bounded as T -> 0) and recover sigma = w/sqrt(T) only at the end. A solver whose state variable is sigma and whose derivative is vega = S*exp(-q*T)*phi(d1)*sqrt(T) must be rejected in code review.

Before solving, validate the target mid against European no-arbitrage bounds and refuse rather than solve if violated: calls must satisfy max(0, S*exp(-q*T) - K*exp(-r*T)) < mid < S*exp(-q*T); puts must satisfy max(0, K*exp(-r*T) - S*exp(-q*T)) < mid < K*exp(-r*T). A violation returns reason code PRICE_OUTSIDE_BOUNDS.

Route every IV solve to the out-of-the-money contract: solve the put when K < F, the call when K >= F, and derive the in-the-money twin via put-call parity C - P = exp(-r*T)*(F - K). Never solve IV directly from an in-the-money American quote.

Obtain the forward F from put-call parity at the strike where |call_mid - put_mid| is smallest, using F = K + exp(r*T)*(call_mid - put_mid), and price with Black-76. Do not model a dividend yield q for SPY/QQQ. If both ATM legs do not have two-sided, uncrossed, non-stale quotes, fall back to F = S*exp(r*T) and set a degraded-forward flag on every downstream greek.

Use a bracketed, safeguarded solver, never bare Newton. Bracket w in [1e-8, w_hi] where w_hi is doubled from an initial guess until the model price exceeds the target or the implied sigma exceeds 5.0 (500%). Accept a Newton step only if it lands strictly inside the current bracket, otherwise bisect. Terminate on |model_price - target| < 0.25 * tick or bracket width < 1e-10, with a hard cap of 50 iterations. Iteration-cap exhaustion returns reason code NO_CONVERGENCE, not the last iterate.

Compute N(x) = 0.5*erfc(-x/sqrt(2)). Polynomial CDF approximations are prohibited. Guard phi(d1) underflow: when phi(d1) == 0.0, set gamma = 0 and vega = 0 explicitly rather than evaluating the ratio, and assert no NaN or Inf leaves the greek function.

Compute and store an IV uncertainty band for every solved IV: iv_band = (ask_mid_half_spread) / vega_per_unit_vol, where vega_per_unit_vol = S*exp(-q*T)*phi(d1)*sqrt(T). Any strategy decision that depends on the IV level (richness, edge, vol-based sizing) must be blocked when iv_band exceeds a configured threshold; a sane starting threshold is 0.02 (2 vol points). Delta/gamma-based decisions are exempt because they are clock- and IV-band-insensitive when IV was solved from the same quote.

Reject the quote before solving if any of: bid <= 0, ask <= 0, bid > ask, quote age > a configured staleness limit (start at 2 seconds intraday), or the option quote timestamp and the underlying quote timestamp differ by more than that limit. Each rejection returns its own reason code.
Use the underlying's NBBO mid, not the last trade, as S, so that S and the option mid are measured consistently. Record both timestamps with every greek row.

Enforce a last-hour regime following Cboe's own VIX1D rule: once business minutes remaining < 60, stop accepting newly solved IV as an input to sizing and instead freeze the last IV solved while minutes >= 60. Position risk in this window must be evaluated from terminal payoff and distance-to-strike, not from theta or vega.

Implement a model-free fallback for probability-of-ITM when the IV solve fails but adjacent same-expiry strikes have two-sided quotes: N(d2) ~ exp(r*T) * (C(K - dK) - C(K + dK)) / (2*dK). Tag the result as MODEL_FREE_PROXY and mark vega, theta and gamma as unavailable (None, never 0) for that contract.

Never fabricate a greek. When IV cannot be solved and the model-free proxy is also unavailable, return None for every greek, block all new entries on that contract, and mark existing positions with worst-case risk assumptions (delta = +/-1.0 if intrinsic > 0, 0.0 otherwise) for margin and sizing purposes. A zero must never stand in for a missing greek.

Never interpolate IV across expirations. When filling a missing IV, interpolate only along the same expiry, in log-moneyness ln(K/F) versus total variance w, and only between strikes whose own solves succeeded and whose iv_band passed the threshold. Refuse to extrapolate beyond the outermost successful strike.

Source the risk-free rate from the U.S. Treasury daily par yield curve (CMT), interpolate with a natural cubic spline on days-to-maturity, and convert BEY -> APY -> continuous as APY = (1 + BEY/2)^2 - 1 then r = ln(1 + APY). Cache per business day. If the rate is older than one business day, allow the 0DTE path to continue (rho * 100bp is about 1.2 cents/share at T = 1 day) but block any 30-45 DTE pricing decision (the same error is about 37 cents/share at 45 DTE) or force it onto the parity-implied forward instead.

Do not implement a binomial or American solver. Instead compute and log the two early-exercise error bounds on every valuation: american_call_premium <= PV(dividends with ex-date strictly before expiry), and american_put_premium <= K*(1 - exp(-r*T)). If either bound exceeds a configured fraction of the option's mid (start at 2%), flag the valuation as EUROPEAN_APPROX_SUSPECT rather than silently using it.

Maintain a hard-coded, validated ex-dividend calendar for every ETF traded. SPY 2026 ex-dates are 2026-03-20, 2026-06-18, 2026-09-18, 2026-12-18 (plus a potential 2026-12-31 excise distribution). The calendar must be re-fetched from the issuer at least quarterly and the fetch failing must raise, not default to 'no dividends'. QQQ's schedule is NOT verified here and must be fetched from Invesco before any QQQ short-call position is opened.

On the last trading session before any ex-dividend date, screen every short call leg: compute remaining_time_value = call_mid - max(0, S - K); if dividend_per_share > remaining_time_value, close the leg or explicitly provision for assignment before the close. This check is independent of the greek engine and must run even when IV solves fail.

Stop opening or extending 0DTE positions no later than 15:25 ET, ahead of Alpaca's documented 15:30 ET cutoff on expiration day. The gate must be wall-clock based and must not depend on any model output.

Run a pre-close expiration sweep that evaluates every expiring position against intrinsic value with a $0.01 threshold (the OCC exercise-by-exception level Alpaca applies), verifies that buying power for call exercise or shares for put exercise are actually present, and closes or submits DNE otherwise. Do not rely on delta to predict whether a contract finishes ITM; use the $0.01 intrinsic test directly.

Every greek row written to storage must carry: the clock tag, T in years, the forward source (parity or spot-compounded), the rate and its as-of date, the IV solve reason code, the iv_band, the underlying and option quote timestamps, and a degraded/fallback flag. A row missing any of these fields must not be consumed by the strategy layer.

Add regression tests that assert the clock invariance identity: for a fixed market mid, solving IV under the calendar clock and under the business clock must produce spot deltas and gammas agreeing to within 1e-6, and IVs whose ratio equals sqrt(525600/102060) to within 1e-6. A failure of this test means the solver and the greek functions are not using the same T.

topic: Alpaca options trading API — precise mechanics for an automated level-3 paper system (US equity/ETF options)

findings.claim: Alpaca option symbols are OCC/OSI symbols with the root NOT space-padded: ROOT + YYMMDD + C|P + 8-digit strike (strike x 1000, zero-padded).
findings.detail: Alpaca docs show `AAPL240119C00100000` = "AAPL Jan 19 2024 100 Call" (19 chars) and `PTON240126C00000500` = PTON $0.50 call, `QS240126P00006500` = QS $6.50 put (17 chars). The canonical OSI spec is 21 chars with the root padded to 6 bytes; Alpaca omits the padding, so symbol length varies with root length. Strike decoding: float(sym[-8:]) / 1000. Type char is at sym[-9]; expiry is sym[-15:-9] as YYMMDD. Do NOT parse from the left by fixed offsets — parse from the RIGHT, because roots are 1-6 chars and non-standard roots exist (e.g. adjusted contracts get roots like AAPL1).
findings.why_it_matters: Any symbol builder/parser must construct and decode from the right, never pad the root to 6, and never assume a fixed total length. A left-anchored parser silently mis-reads every ticker whose root isn't 4 characters.

findings.claim: Do not build option symbols yourself for trading. Resolve them from GET /v2/options/contracts and trade only contracts with tradable=true and status=active.
findings.detail: Alpaca returns explicit submit errors for `contract "{symbol}" not found`, `is not active`, `is not tradable`, `is expired`, `expires soon, unable to open new positions`, and `invalid contract` (all HTTP 422, code 42210000). Adjusted/non-standard contracts (post corporate action) have different roots, deliverables and multipliers, and a hand-built symbol will either 404 or hit a contract whose multiplier is not 100.
findings.why_it_matters: The order path must take the exact `symbol` string returned by the contracts endpoint as its input, not a string it composed. Symbol construction is allowed only for building a lookup filter, never as the traded identifier.

findings.claim: GET /v2/options/contracts defaults silently hide most of the chain: expiration_date_lte defaults to 'next weekend' and limit defaults to 100 (max 10000).
findings.detail: Query params (all optional): underlying_symbols (comma-separated, e.g. 'AAPL,SPY'), show_deliverables (bool), status (active|inactive, default active), expiration_date (YYYY-MM-DD), expiration_date_gte, expiration_date_lte (DEFAULT = next weekend), root_symbol, type (call|put), style (american|european), strike_price_gte, strike_price_lte, ppind (bool), limit (default 100, max 10000), page_token. Single contract: GET /v2/options/contracts/{symbol_or_id}. Response contract fields: id, symbol, name, status, tradable, expiration_date, root_symbol, underlying_symbol, underlying_asset_id, type, style, strike_price, multiplier, size, open_interest, open_interest_date, close_price, close_price_date, optional deliverables[].
findings.why_it_matters: If the scanner does not set expiration_date_gte/lte and limit explicitly and follow pagination, it will see a truncated, date-clipped chain and conclude strikes don't exist. Every contracts query must set both date bounds and loop on the page token.

findings.claim: The contracts response pagination field name is documented inconsistently: OpenAPI says `next_page_token`, the narrative doc example shows `page_token`.
findings.detail: OpenAPI schema for the list response declares `option_contracts[]` plus `next_page_token`. The Options Trading doc's worked example shows a body ending `"page_token": "MTAw", "limit": 100`. The request parameter is `page_token` in both.
findings.why_it_matters: The pagination loop must read `next_page_token or page_token` and stop on null/empty, otherwise it either infinite-loops or stops after page 1 depending on which shape the API actually returns.

findings.claim: Use the contract's `multiplier` for money math, never `size`. Alpaca explicitly says size is not a multiplier.
findings.detail: OpenAPI: multiplier — "In standard contracts, the multiplier is always set to 100... if a contract is traded at $1.50 and the multiplier is 100, the total amount debited would be $150.00." size — "the number of underlying shares to be delivered in case the contract is exercised/assigned... This field should **not** be used as a multiplier, specially for non-standard contracts." Both are required fields on the contract object.
findings.why_it_matters: Premium, cost-basis, and risk math must read contract.multiplier per contract. For adjusted contracts size != multiplier and hardcoding 100 produces wrong sizing and wrong max-loss on exactly the contracts where being wrong is most expensive.

findings.claim: Single-leg option orders go to the same POST /v2/orders endpoint as equities, with hard validations: qty must be a whole number, notional must not be set, extended_hours must be false/absent, time_in_force must be day or gtc, type must be market, limit, stop or stop_limit.
findings.detail: Verbatim from Alpaca's Options Trading page: "Ensuring `qty` is a whole number; `Notional` must not be populated; `time_in_force` must be `day` or `gtc`; `extended_hours` must be `false` or not populated; `type` must be `market`,`limit`,`stop` or `stop_limit` (`stop` and `stop_limit` are only available for single-leg orders)". The OpenAPI TimeInForce description confirms: "Options trading: day, gtc." trailing_stop is equity-only.
findings.why_it_matters: The order builder must whitelist per asset class: reject opg/cls/ioc/fok/trailing_stop/notional/fractional/extended_hours before the request leaves the process, so a bad config fails loudly in code rather than as an opaque 422 mid-session.

findings.claim: Multi-leg orders support ONLY market and limit — stop and stop_limit are single-leg only — and there is no bracket/OCO/OTO for options at all.
findings.detail: OpenAPI OrderType description, verbatim: "Equity trading: market, limit, stop, stop_limit, trailing_stop. Options trading: market, limit, stop, stop_limit. Multileg Options trading: market, limit." OrderClass description: "Options trading: simple (or \"\"), mleg (required for multi-leg complex option strategies)." A submit error exists for `complex orders not supported for options trading` (422/42210000). alpaca-py enforces the same: "mleg order class only supports market and limit orders."
findings.why_it_matters: There is NO broker-side stop-loss or take-profit attached to a spread. Any protective exit on a multi-leg position must be implemented as bot-side monitoring plus a new closing mleg order. The system must never assume a resting stop exists on a spread.

findings.claim: Max legs is 4 (enforced in the OpenAPI schema); min legs is 2 (enforced in the SDK, not in the published OpenAPI).
findings.detail: OpenAPI CreateOrderRequest: legs — "list of order legs (<= 4)", "maxItems": 4. alpaca-py raises "At most 4 legs are allowed for the mleg order class", "At least 2 legs are required for the mleg order class", and "All legs must have unique symbols". The minimum-2 and unique-symbol rules are SDK-level; I did not find them stated in Alpaca's server-side docs, so treat them as strong but not doc-confirmed.
findings.why_it_matters: Validate 2 <= len(legs) <= 4 and all leg symbols distinct before submitting; this caps the strategy universe to verticals, iron condors/butterflies (4 legs), straddles/strangles — no 6-leg structures, no legging a 4-leg condor plus an extra hedge in one order.

findings.claim: For order_class=mleg: `symbol` must be OMITTED at top level, `qty` is REQUIRED and means number of strategy units, and each leg carries {symbol, ratio_qty, side, position_intent}.
findings.detail: OpenAPI: symbol — "required for all order classes except for `mleg`"; qty — "Required for `mleg` order class, represents the number of units to trade of this strategy". MLegOrderLeg required fields are symbol and ratio_qty; side and position_intent are individually optional in the schema but Alpaca returns `leg.{i} position intent is required` (422) and alpaca-py requires at least one of side/position_intent. Executed leg quantity = parent qty x ratio_qty. PositionIntent enum: buy_to_open, buy_to_close, sell_to_open, sell_to_close.
findings.why_it_matters: Always send position_intent on every leg explicitly. A single-leg order also accepts top-level position_intent, and Alpaca will reject a mismatch with `position intent mismatch, inferred: {x}, specified: {y}` — so the intent your strategy state machine believes must be the intent you transmit.

findings.claim: On an mleg limit order, limit_price is a NET price where positive = debit and negative = CREDIT.
findings.detail: OpenAPI limit_price, verbatim: "In case of `mleg`, the limit_price parameter is expressed with the following notation: A positive value indicates a debit, representing a cost or payment to be made. A negative value signifies a credit, reflecting an amount to be received." All of Alpaca's own level-3 examples (including the iron condor) pass a positive number; the credit case is documented only in the schema.
findings.why_it_matters: A credit spread submitted with a positive limit_price is an order to PAY that amount instead of receive it — a silent, potentially unbounded pricing inversion. The code must compute net price with signed leg contributions and assert sign(limit_price) matches the strategy's intended debit/credit before sending.

findings.claim: ratio_qty values must be coprime — Alpaca rejects any leg-ratio set whose GCD is not 1.
findings.detail: Verbatim: "each leg's `leg_ratio` must be in its simplest form. In other words, the greatest common divisor (GCD) among the `leg_ratio` values for the legs must be 1... If a ratio must be 2:4, the user should enter it as 1:2." A 4:2 ratio is rejected outright.
findings.why_it_matters: Normalize: divide all ratio_qty by their GCD and multiply the parent qty by that GCD. Equal-ratio strategies (verticals, condors) must use ratio_qty=1 on every leg, with size carried entirely by qty.

findings.claim: Alpaca's option approval levels are 0-3 only. There is NO level 4 at Alpaca — the account field is an enum of {0,1,2,3}.
findings.detail: Trading Account OpenAPI: options_approved_level and options_trading_level both have enum [0,1,2,3] with description "0=disabled, 1=Covered Call/Cash-Secured Put, 2=Long Call/Put, 3=Spreads/Straddles." Account configuration max_options_trading_level has the same 0-3 enum. options_trading_level = min(options_approved_level, max_options_trading_level). Alpaca's support page lists three tiers and no fourth. Industry "level 4 = naked writing" does not exist here.
findings.why_it_matters: Level 3 is the ceiling. Any strategy that at other brokers would need level 4 (naked short calls, naked short puts beyond cash-secured, short straddles/strangles) is permanently unavailable and must be excluded at strategy-selection time, not discovered at order rejection.

findings.claim: What level 3 permits and — precisely — what it forbids.
findings.detail: Permitted: everything in L1 (sell covered call — requires owning 100 x qty shares; sell cash-secured put — requires full strike x multiplier x qty buying power), everything in L2 (buy call, buy put), plus defined-risk spreads: debit and credit verticals, iron condors, iron butterflies, straddles/strangles as LONG structures, and rolls of spreads. FORBIDDEN at level 3: (a) any uncovered/naked short option — Alpaca's own submit errors are `account not eligible to trade uncovered option contracts` and `account not eligible to trade spreads or uncovered contracts`; (b) within a single mleg order, ANY leg not covered inside that same order — verbatim: "an MLeg order is accepted only if all its legs are covered within the same MLeg order. For example, an MLeg order containing two short call legs would be rejected... This restriction also impacts certain strategies, including rolling a short contract or rolling a calendar spread, since they would involve uncovered short legs within the same multi-leg order."; (c) short straddles/strangles (uncovered by construction); (d) naked calendars/diagonals as a single mleg (the short leg is not covered within that order because the long has a different expiry).
findings.why_it_matters: The strategy whitelist must be enumerated in code and checked before order construction: every short leg must have an offsetting long of the SAME expiration, same underlying, and protective strike, inside the same order. Calendars and diagonals must be rejected or legged in separately (accepting leg risk), and rolling a short single is not a legal mleg.

findings.claim: Alpaca's own two level-3 descriptions disagree on scope; the narrower published table says only 'Buy a call spread / Buy a put spread'.
findings.detail: The Options Trading and Options Trading Overview level tables list Level 3 as "Options Level 1 and 2 Strategies + Buy a call spread + Buy a put spread" — debit spreads only, on its face. The Options Level 3 Trading page, the account-model description ("3=Spreads/Straddles") and the support page all describe a broader set, and Alpaca's own cost-basis worked example on the level-3 page is a CALL CREDIT SPREAD. The broader reading is almost certainly correct, but the tables have not been updated.
findings.why_it_matters: Do not treat the doc as a reliable permission oracle. The system must probe permissions empirically once per strategy family (submit a minimum-size order in paper, record accept/reject and the error code) and keep a persisted whitelist, rather than assuming the doc table.

findings.claim: Whether an equity leg can appear in an mleg order is genuinely contradictory in current Alpaca docs.
findings.detail: The Options Level 3 Trading page states verbatim: "MLeg orders that include an equity leg are not supported at this time. This means that combining an equity position with an options contract in a single order is not currently available for any trading strategy." But the multi-leg submit error table (a newer page) contains `equity legs are allowed only with a corresponding amount of call contracts` — a rule that only makes sense if equity legs are accepted in some form (buy-write). The level-3 page was last updated ~12 months ago.
findings.why_it_matters: This cannot be resolved from the docs. The system must not depend on stock+option combos in one order. If a buy-write is ever wanted, probe it in paper first and treat the result as authoritative; otherwise submit the stock and the option as separate orders and accept the leg risk.

findings.claim: Margin/cost basis for spreads uses a piecewise-payoff 'universal spread rule' (worst-case net payoff across all strikes, per expiration), not per-pair spread margin.
findings.detail: Alpaca: maintenance margin ignores premiums, models each option's intrinsic payoff as a piecewise-linear function of underlying price p, sums them across ALL open positions, and takes the absolute value of the most negative point. "For option positions with multiple expiration dates, calculate this theoretical maximum-loss approach separately for each expiration date, then use the largest resulting requirement across all expirations." Cost basis charged for an mleg order = maintenance margin (universal spread rule) + net price x multiplier, where a credit reduces it. Worked example: long 200C / short 190C credit spread = $1,000 margin + (-$5 x 100) = $500 charged. Alpaca cites the Cboe Margin Manual and SR-CBOE-2012-043 as the basis.
findings.why_it_matters: Pre-trade capital checks must evaluate the WHOLE portfolio's worst-case payoff per expiration, not the new spread in isolation — a new position can require less than its standalone max loss (offsets) or interact with existing positions. Sizing that assumes 'margin = strike width x 100 x qty' will over-reserve, and sizing that ignores same-expiry interactions can under-reserve.

findings.claim: options_buying_power is a separate account field from buying_power and is the one checked when opening option positions.
findings.detail: Trading account model carries buying_power, regt_buying_power, non_marginable_buying_power, daytrading_buying_power, multiplier (1/2/4), maintenance_margin, AND options_buying_power ("Your buying power for options trading"), plus options_approved_level / options_trading_level. Rejection payloads carry structured extras: `{"options_buying_power":"7267.84","code":40310000,"cost_basis":"38000","message":"insufficient options buying power"}`; covered-call rejection carries available_qty/required_qty/underlying_asset_id; CSP rejection carries required_options_buying_power.
findings.why_it_matters: Pre-trade sizing must read options_buying_power, not buying_power, and must parse the structured fields off the 403 body rather than regex the message string (Alpaca states the message text can change without notice; the numeric code and HTTP status are the stable contract).

findings.claim: Option positions appear in GET /v2/positions with asset_class = 'us_option', qty in CONTRACTS, current_price per share, and NO multiplier field.
findings.detail: Real example from the docs: {"symbol":"PTON240126C00000500", "asset_class":"us_option", "asset_marginable":true, "qty":"2", "avg_entry_price":"6.05", "side":"long", "market_value":"1068", "cost_basis":"1210", "current_price":"5.34", "qty_available":"2", "exchange":""}. Note 2 x 5.34 x 100 = 1068, so market_value already includes the multiplier while current_price does not. asset_id is the option contract ID. `exchange` is empty for options. qty_available = "Total number of shares available minus open orders / locked for options covered call". The Position schema has no multiplier and no expiration/strike/type fields.
findings.why_it_matters: Position-level risk code must not multiply market_value by 100, must multiply current_price by qty x multiplier, must look up expiry/strike/type by calling the contracts endpoint (or parsing the symbol), and must use qty_available — not qty — before selling, because shares/contracts pledged to a covered call are locked. Short option positions show side='short' with negative qty; cover-checking logic must handle the sign.

findings.claim: Exercise is POST /v2/positions/{symbol_or_contract_id}/exercise with NO body, and it exercises the ENTIRE position — there is no qty parameter.
findings.detail: Verbatim: "All available held shares of this option contract will be exercised... Exercise requests will be processed immediately once received. Exercise requests submitted between market close and midnight will be rejected." Documented rejections (403/40310000) include: `exercise requests are not accepted after market close until midnight`, `early exercise is not allowed for European-style options`, `insufficient cash available`, `insufficient regt buying power`, `insufficient underlying qty available for deliverable`, `cannot exercise position marked as do-not-exercise`, `you are attempting to exercise an out of the money option contract, please contact support`, `you are attempting to exercise a non-standard option contract, please contact support`; 404/40410000 `long position not found`. DNE is a separate endpoint (docs also say contact support). Activities: OPEXC (removes the option position) + OPTRD (the paired trade); assignment produces OPASN + OPTRD.
findings.why_it_matters: The call is all-or-nothing and irreversible. A bot must never call it as a routine exit — closing by selling the contract is the normal path. If it is called, it must first verify ITM, American style, sufficient cash/regt buying power for the full deliverable, and that the clock is inside market hours.

findings.claim: Expiration-day behaviour is broker-driven and starts at 3:30pm ET: Alpaca stops accepting opening orders on same-day expiries and auto-exercises ITM-by-$0.01 longs, or liquidates them if buying power is short.
findings.detail: Verbatim: "Starting at 3:30 pm EST on the date of expiration, Alpaca continuously evaluates any open positions that expire that day and stops accepting new orders to open/extend any positions." ITM by >= $0.01: auto-exercise if the account can support it, otherwise "Alpaca will liquidate while it's still ITM" (the Options Trading page says it will sell out the position within 1 hour before expiry). Covered calls / CSPs ITM by >= $0.01 are automatically assigned after close. OTM/ATM generally expire worthless, but "positions slightly OTM may also be liquidated depending on market and underlying conditions." There is also a submit error `exceeded account limit for contracts expiring today (requested, held+open, limit)` — an undisclosed 0DTE position cap.
findings.why_it_matters: An automated system holding 0DTE must treat 15:30 ET as a hard wall for opening, must model forced liquidation/exercise as an exogenous event that changes positions without any order it placed, and must poll positions after 15:30 rather than trust its own order book. The 0DTE contract limit value is not published — the code must handle that rejection gracefully and back off.

findings.claim: Assignment is NOT pushed over websocket — option non-trade activities must be polled from the REST activities endpoint, and on paper they are delayed a full day.
findings.detail: Verbatim: "Options assignments are not delivered through websocket events. To check for assignment activity (non-trade activity, or NTA events), you'll need to poll the REST API endpoints. Websocket support for NTAs is not currently available." And, for paper specifically: "On PAPER NTAs are synced at the start of the following day. While your balance and positions are updated instantly, NTAs on PAPER will be visible in the Activities endpoint only the next day." There is also an `active assignment lock on {symbol}, cannot close all long options` rejection.
findings.why_it_matters: Assignment/exercise/expiry detection in paper CANNOT be built on the activities feed — it must be built on diffing /v2/positions and /v2/account against the bot's own expected state. The trade stream alone will silently miss assignment, and reconciliation logic that waits for OPASN will hang for a day.

findings.claim: Options market orders are rejected outside market hours, and day orders submitted after the close are queued to the next session.
findings.detail: Submit error (422/42210000): `options market orders are only allowed during market hours`. Separately the TimeInForce doc for `day`: "If submitted after the close, it is queued and submitted the following trading day." extended_hours is rejected for options entirely (`extended hours is not supported for options trading`).
findings.why_it_matters: A bot that fires a market order at 16:05 gets a rejection; one that fires a day LIMIT order at 16:05 gets something worse — a live order at tomorrow's open, priced on stale data. Every order path must gate on a clock/calendar check and refuse to submit outside 09:30-16:00 ET unless the strategy explicitly intends a next-session order.

findings.claim: Cancel and replace of mleg orders may be disabled at the account/firm level, and there is a documented per-order qty cap whose value Alpaca does not publish.
findings.detail: Error tables include 403/40310000 `submit mleg order is disabled`, `cancel mleg order is disabled`, `replace mleg order is disabled`. Also 422 `options order qty must be <= {max}` and `options order notional is {n} must be <= {limit}` — both limits are runtime-substituted and not documented anywhere I could find. Replace additionally errors on `order chain not fully replaced`, `order parameters are not changed`, `qty must be > filled_qty`.
findings.why_it_matters: The exit path must not assume replace works on a spread. Implement cancel-then-resubmit as the primary re-pricing mechanism, treat replace as a best-effort optimisation, and treat a 403 'disabled' as a kill-switch condition for that strategy rather than a retryable error. Per-order qty caps must be discovered by probing and then hardcoded conservatively.

findings.claim: How paper simulates MULTI-LEG option fills is not documented — this is a real blind spot.
findings.detail: The Paper Trading page never mentions options. Its documented rules are equity-framed: orders fill only when marketable against NBBO; order size is not checked against NBBO quantity ("you can submit and receive a fill for an order that is much larger than the actual available liquidity"); eligible orders get a random partial fill 10% of the time; no dividends simulated; account balance fixed unless reset. Nothing states whether an mleg net limit is evaluated against the net NBBO of the combination, against each leg independently, or whether legs can partially fill against each other.
findings.why_it_matters: Paper backtest/forward-test results on spreads are not trustworthy as fill-quality evidence, and any strategy whose edge comes from getting filled near the mid on a 4-leg structure is unvalidated. The system should log requested vs filled net price on every mleg and treat paper P&L as an upper bound. Do not size live capital off paper option fills.

findings.claim: In paper, options trading is enabled by default; live requires an approval flow, and the effective level can be capped below the approved level.
findings.detail: Verbatim: "In the Paper environment, options trading capability will be enabled by default - there's nothing you need to do! Note, in production there will be a more robust experience to request options trading." Live approval statuses are APPROVED / LOWER_LEVEL_APPROVED / REJECTED. options_trading_level = min(options_approved_level, account_configurations.max_options_trading_level), so a user or an errant config PATCH can silently downgrade the bot's permissions.
findings.why_it_matters: The bot must read options_trading_level (the EFFECTIVE one) at startup and periodically, not options_approved_level, and must halt any strategy family above the level it actually observes — a paper->live promotion is where a level assumption turns into rejected orders or, worse, a half-built spread.

findings.claim: European-style legs in one mleg must share an expiration date, and index options carry extra timing rules — relevant only if the universe ever widens beyond equities/ETFs.
findings.detail: Errors: 422 `European-style option legs in a multi-leg order must have the same expiration date`; `orders for morning-expiration index options cannot be placed on expiration day`; `orders for morning-expiration index options cannot be placed after market close when expiration is the next trading day`. Exercise: `early exercise is not allowed for European-style options`. US listed equity/ETF options are American-style and share-settled, per Alpaca ("US listed equities options, all american style").
findings.why_it_matters: Filter the tradable universe on contract.style == 'american' if the design assumes share settlement and early-exercise/assignment risk. If style == 'european' ever appears, settlement is cash and the assignment model in code is wrong.

findings.claim: Error handling contract: match on numeric code + HTTP status, never on message text.
findings.detail: Alpaca states verbatim: "The `message` strings can change without notice. The numeric `code` and HTTP status are the stable contract. Placeholders in curly braces are substituted at runtime." Options codes: 40310000 (403, permission/buying-power/eligibility), 42210000 (422, validation), 40410000 (404, not found).
findings.why_it_matters: Error classification must key on (status, code) and then on structured extra fields in the body (options_buying_power, required_qty, available_qty, cost_basis). String matching on messages is guaranteed to rot.

rules_for_the_machine: SYMBOLS — Never trade a symbol the bot composed. The only tradable symbol string is one returned by GET /v2/options/contracts (or /v2/options/contracts/{symbol_or_id}). Composition is permitted only to build a filter.

SYMBOLS — Parse OCC symbols from the RIGHT: strike = int(sym[-8:]) / 1000; right = 'C' or 'P' at sym[-9]; expiry = datetime.strptime(sym[-15:-9], '%y%m%d'); root = sym[:-15]. Assert len(sym) >= 16 and sym[-9] in 'CP' and sym[-8:].isdigit(). Never pad the root to 6 chars; never index from the left.

CONTRACTS — Every contracts query must explicitly set expiration_date_gte AND expiration_date_lte (the server default silently clips to 'next weekend') and limit (default 100, max 10000), and must loop on pagination reading `next_page_token or page_token`, stopping on null/empty, with a hard cap on iterations.
CONTRACTS — Reject any contract where tradable is not true or status != 'active'. Reject any contract where style != 'american' unless the strategy explicitly handles cash settlement.

CONTRACTS — Reject any contract where multiplier != '100' or size != multiplier, unless an explicit 'allow_adjusted_contracts' flag is set. Use contract.multiplier (never size, never a hardcoded 100) in every premium, cost-basis and max-loss calculation.

ORDER BUILDER — Whitelist per asset class before transmit. For options: reject notional, reject fractional qty (assert qty == int(qty) and qty >= 1), reject extended_hours=True, reject time_in_force not in {'day','gtc'}, reject order type not in {'market','limit','stop','stop_limit'}.

ORDER BUILDER — For order_class='mleg': reject type not in {'market','limit'}; reject stop_price/trail_price/trail_percent; reject take_profit/stop_loss blocks. Bracket/OCO/OTO are equity-only and must be rejected for any option order.

MLEG — Assert 2 <= len(legs) <= 4, all leg symbols distinct, all legs share the same underlying_symbol, and gcd(all ratio_qty) == 1 (normalize by dividing ratios by the GCD and multiplying parent qty by it).

MLEG — Omit top-level `symbol` and `side` entirely; set top-level `qty` (required, integer >= 1, = number of strategy units). Executed leg contracts = qty * ratio_qty; assert that product against sizing limits per leg, not just per order.

MLEG — Set `position_intent` explicitly on EVERY leg (buy_to_open | buy_to_close | sell_to_open | sell_to_close). Derive it from the bot's own position ledger, then assert it agrees with the live /v2/positions state before transmit, to avoid 'position intent mismatch'.

MLEG PRICING — Compute net price as sum over legs of (sign * ratio_qty * leg_price), sign = +1 for buy, -1 for sell. Submit limit_price with that sign convention: POSITIVE = debit, NEGATIVE = credit. Assert sign(limit_price) == expected sign for the strategy (credit spreads MUST send a negative limit_price) and refuse to transmit on mismatch.

MLEG PRICING — Bound the limit price: refuse to submit if abs(limit_price) exceeds the strategy's theoretical max (e.g. a vertical's net debit must be < strike_width) or if the quoted net bid/ask spread exceeds a configured max (reject illiquid structures rather than crossing a wide market).

LEVEL 3 GATE — Read account.options_trading_level (the EFFECTIVE min of approved and max_options_trading_level) at startup and at least once per session. Halt all option activity if it is < the level the running strategy requires. Never key off options_approved_level.

LEVEL 3 GATE — Hard-reject, in code, before order construction: any naked/uncovered short option; any short straddle or strangle; any single-leg sell_to_open that is not (a) a covered call with >= 100*qty shares in qty_available of the underlying, or (b) a cash-secured put with strike*multiplier*qty of options_buying_power reserved.

LEVEL 3 GATE — For every mleg order, verify coverage INSIDE that order: each short leg must be matched by a long leg of the same underlying, the same expiration date, and a protective strike (long call strike <= short call strike offset for debit structures; long put strike <= short put strike; condors: both wings present). Reject calendars, diagonals, and 'roll a naked short' as mleg — Alpaca rejects them and a partial workaround by legging must be an explicit, separately-flagged code path.

LEVEL 3 GATE — Do not put an equity leg in an mleg order. The docs contradict themselves on whether it is allowed; treat it as forbidden. Buy-writes must be two separate orders with explicit leg-risk handling.

PERMISSIONS DISCOVERY — Maintain a persisted per-strategy-family whitelist populated by one-contract probe orders in paper, keyed on (status, code) of the response. Treat 403/40310000 with an eligibility message as a permanent disable for that family until a human re-enables it; never retry it in a loop.

CAPITAL — Size from account.options_buying_power, not buying_power. Reserve, per order, at least the universal-spread-rule maintenance margin plus the net debit (credits reduce it), and re-read options_buying_power after every fill rather than decrementing a local estimate.

CAPITAL — Compute pre-trade risk as the worst-case piecewise net payoff of (existing positions + proposed position) evaluated at every strike present, per expiration date, taking the max requirement across expirations — not as the standalone max loss of the new spread. Block the order if that portfolio worst case breaches the configured account-level loss cap.

ERRORS — Classify on (HTTP status, numeric code) only: 403/40310000 = permission or buying power, 422/42210000 = validation, 40410000 = not found. Never regex the message. Extract structured extras (options_buying_power, cost_basis, required_qty, available_qty, required_options_buying_power) from the JSON body for logging and sizing.
ERRORS — Treat `submit mleg order is disabled`, `cancel mleg order is disabled`, `replace mleg order is disabled` (403) as kill-switch conditions: stop the strategy, alert, do not retry.

CLOCK — Gate every option order on the market clock/calendar. Market orders: refuse outside 09:30-16:00 ET (Alpaca rejects them). Limit/day orders: refuse after the close unless the strategy explicitly intends a next-session order, because a day order submitted after close is queued to the following trading day.
CLOCK — Hard stop: do not submit any opening or position-extending order on a contract expiring today after 15:30 ET. Alpaca stops accepting them and the bot's own state will diverge.

EXITS — Never assume a broker-side stop exists on a multi-leg position. Every spread must be paired with a bot-side monitor that submits a closing mleg order (or per-leg orders) when its exit condition triggers, with a heartbeat that alerts if the monitor stops running while the position is open.

EXITS — Prefer cancel-then-resubmit over PATCH replace for re-pricing option orders; treat replace as best-effort and handle 'order parameters are not changed', 'order chain not fully replaced', 'qty must be > filled_qty' as non-fatal no-ops.

POSITIONS — Identify option positions by asset_class == 'us_option'. qty is CONTRACTS. market_value already includes the multiplier; current_price does not. Never multiply market_value by 100. Expiry/strike/type are absent from the position object — get them from the contract record.
POSITIONS — Always check qty_available (not qty) before submitting a closing/covering order; shares and contracts locked against a covered call or an open order are excluded from qty_available.

RECONCILIATION — Detect exercise, assignment and expiry by diffing /v2/positions and /v2/account against the bot's expected state on a schedule, NOT by waiting for activities or websocket events: assignments are never pushed over websocket, and on paper all option NTAs appear only the next day.

RECONCILIATION — After 15:30 ET on any expiration date the bot holds, poll positions at least every few minutes until flat: Alpaca may auto-exercise, auto-assign, or force-liquidate positions with no order from the bot, including positions 'slightly OTM'.

EXERCISE — Do not call POST /v2/positions/{symbol_or_contract_id}/exercise as a routine exit; close by trading the contract. If exercising at all: require an explicit config flag, verify the position is long, American-style, ITM, inside market hours, and that cash/regt buying power covers strike*multiplier*full position qty — the call has no qty parameter and exercises the ENTIRE position irreversibly.

0DTE — Handle 'exceeded account limit for contracts expiring today' (403/40310000) as a hard per-account cap whose value Alpaca does not publish: parse the returned limit, persist it, and cap same-day-expiry contract counts below it thereafter. Do not retry blindly.

PAPER — Log requested vs filled net price and fill latency on every option order, and treat paper fill quality as an upper bound, not evidence. Alpaca's paper engine does not check size against NBBO depth, partial-fills randomly ~10% of the time, and has no documented multi-leg fill model. Do not size live capital from paper option P&L.

IDEMPOTENCY — Set a deterministic client_order_id (<= 128 chars) on every option order, derived from strategy + underlying + expiry + strikes + intent + timestamp bucket, so a retry after a timeout cannot double-open a spread.
